For fungal nail infection, the capsule label prohibits use with ventricular dysfunction or a history of heart failure, and during pregnancy or when pregnancy is planned. Other indications require the separate cardiac risk assessment below.
locator: Contraindications: Congestive Heart Failure; pregnancy paragraph

text: For other indications, ventricular dysfunction requires a benefit that clearly outweighs risk. Active liver disease, abnormal liver enzymes or prior drug-related liver toxicity strongly discourage use unless the situation is serious or life-threatening and benefit exceeds risk.
locator: Warnings: Cardiac Disease; Precautions: Hepatic Impairment

text: Pregnancy and breastfeeding require a separate benefit-risk assessment. An oncology pharmacist should review the complete regimen: contraindicated combinations differ from combinations needing adjustment or monitoring.
locator: Precautions: Pregnancy; Nursing Mothers; Drug Interactions

Starting metformin at eGFR 30-45 mL/min/1.73 m² is not recommended. This is different from the formal contraindication below 30. eGFR estimates kidney filtration.
locator: 2.3 Recommendations for Use in Renal Impairment

text: The label advises avoiding use with hepatic disease. Hypoxic illness, excessive alcohol, restricted food/fluid intake around procedures, and certain contrast studies raise lactic-acidosis concerns or require a clinician-directed temporary hold.

Insulin or insulin-releasing medicines increase hypoglycemia risk. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors and drugs that reduce metformin clearance can increase acidosis or accumulation risks. These are interaction precautions, not universal contraindications.
